This file provides an example how a Bayesian VAR network analysis for depression would work. It also provides an app in which users can compare the networks between a group of individuals and an individual from that group. This allows

The document proceeds as follows:

1.  Data simulation: a group-level VAR network and an individual-level VAR network are simulated based on many individuals' data

2.  Analysis: A sensitivity analysis is conducted, after which the edge of interest (sleep_lag1 -\> tired) under each model is extracted. Then a plot showing how P1’s estimated sleep → tired coefficient changes across three prior settings is given. It is a prior-sensitivity plot. Finally, the differences between the group and individual estimates are calculated, and each difference score's 90% CI is given.

3.  App: The app can be opened, and the user can either input their own data or generate a random participant dataset to compare the individual's network and edges to those of the group

## 2. Simulate data

**1) Set the simulation size**

```{r}
set.seed(2026)  

N <- 25    
Tt <- 100  
p <- 9  
symptoms <- c(
  "down", "tired", "sleep",
  "anhedonia", "worthlessness", "concentration",
  "appetite", "psychomotor", "suicidal"
)
Phi_group <- matrix(
  0,
  nrow = p,
  ncol = p,
  dimnames = list(symptoms, symptoms)
)
diag(Phi_group) <- c(
  0.30, 0.30, 0.35,
  0.30, 0.35, 0.30,
  0.30, 0.30, 0.30
)
Phi_group["down", "sleep"] <- 0.25
Phi_group["down", "tired"] <- 0.15
Phi_group["anhedonia", "worthlessness"] <- 0.20
Phi_group["worthlessness", "anhedonia"] <- 0.15
Phi_group["concentration", "worthlessness"] <- 0.15
Phi_group["tired", "appetite"] <- 0.15
Phi_group["tired", "psychomotor"] <- 0.15
Phi_group["suicidal", "worthlessness"] <- 0.20
Phi_group["down", "suicidal"] <- 0.15

Tau <- matrix(
  0.08,
  nrow = p,
  ncol = p,
  dimnames = list(symptoms, symptoms)
)

Tau["anhedonia", "worthlessness"] <- 0.15

stationary <- function(M) {
  max(Mod(eigen(M, only.values = TRUE)$values)) < 0.95
}

mu <- 1.5
innov_sd <- 0.70

long <- vector("list", N)

for (i in seq_len(N)) {

  repeat {
    U <- matrix(
      rnorm(p * p, mean = 0, sd = as.vector(Tau)),
      nrow = p,
      ncol = p
    )
    Phi_i <- Phi_group + U
    if (i == 1) {
      Phi_i["down", "sleep"] <- 0.00
      Phi_i["anhedonia", "worthlessness"] <- 0.45
      Phi_i["concentration", "anhedonia"] <- 0.30
      Phi_i["suicidal", "worthlessness"] <- 0.35
    }
    if (stationary(Phi_i)) break
  }
  Y <- matrix(0, nrow = Tt, ncol = p)
  Y[1, ] <- rnorm(p, mean = 0, sd = innov_sd)

  for (t in 2:Tt) {
    Y[t, ] <- Phi_i %*% Y[t - 1, ] +
      rnorm(p, mean = 0, sd = innov_sd)
  }
  obs <- round(mu + Y)
  obs[obs < 0] <- 0
  obs[obs > 3] <- 3
  long[[i]] <- data.frame(
    id = i,
    day = 1:Tt,
    obs
  )
}
ema <- do.call(rbind, long)
colnames(ema) <- c("id", "day", symptoms)

stopifnot(nrow(ema) == N * Tt)
stopifnot(all(c("id", "day", symptoms) %in% names(ema)))
stopifnot(all(as.matrix(ema[, symptoms]) %in% 0:3))

rating_frequencies <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(symptoms, function(s) {

    counts <- table(
      factor(ema[[s]], levels = 0:3)
    )

    data.frame(
      symptom = s,
      rating = 0:3,
      count = as.integer(counts),
      proportion = as.integer(counts) / nrow(ema)
    )
  })
)

print(rating_frequencies)

boundary_frequencies <- rating_frequencies[
  rating_frequencies$rating %in% c(0, 3),
]

print(boundary_frequencies)

ratings_per_symptom <- aggregate(
  count ~ symptom,
  data = rating_frequencies,
  FUN = sum
)
stopifnot(all(ratings_per_symptom$count == N * Tt))

dir.create("data", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

write.csv(
  ema,
  "data/ema_simulated.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  rating_frequencies,
  "data/rating_frequencies.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

```
